The 2027 Aura Beachy 420 Is a Compact Travel Trailer With an Unusual Layout and Cool Features
22 photos
Photo: Hobby Caravan
The RV equivalent of "how much you can do with a tiny thing" is the Beachy 420, one of the four flooplans available in the Beachy series of travel trailers – or caravans, as they're called in Europe. The Beachy 420 is perhaps the best choice for an example, since it's a family-friendly unit in a very small form factor.
It's not the tiniest out there, to be sure, but it might be if you consider its versatility and extended functionality. The Beachy 420 is the first entry in the Beachy series that offers real family-friendliness, with a super-size king bed at the back that will fit three adults or two adults and as many as two kids.
And that's not even the most impressive thing about the Beachy 420. That would be its versatility, its openness and degree of comfort, and the vibe that's perfectly matches its name and intended purpose. Out of all compact caravans in Europe, the Beachy is perhaps the most stylish and beautiful.
The Beachy line was launched German specialist Hobby in 2021, first as a concept and then as production models for the 2022 year. For 2027, Beachy is making a move across the pond, getting its official launch in the UK at the 2026 Motorhome & Caravan Show at NEC Birmingham, where the video tour at the bottom of the page was shot.
Photo: Hobby Caravan It won't be called Hobby Beachy , though, but Aura Beachy. Aura is "A brand for Britain [but] made in Germany," the name under which Hobby will be selling products here. An Aura Beach is the same Hobby Beachy that's been a fan favorite across Europe for years, but in slightly different, Aura-branded clothes.
Not that this should stop us from taking the Beachy 420 in – or revisiting it, if you're already familiar with it.
"Could you do with a little bit more?" Hobby asks in the presentation for the Europe-bound Beachy 420, before promising more storage space and one additional berth, both of which they deliver. The Aura description of the UK variant is less enticing , but with a product as nice as this one, it probably doesn't even have to be that.
Photo: Aura Campervans The Beachy 420 is built on a single-axle KNOTT chassis, with an overrun brake with automatic adjustment, hitch stabilizer, shock absorbers, and extendable heavy-duty corner steadies. It's licensed for highway use (for up to 100 kph/62 mph) and it's built with bonded sandwich panels for frameless structural integrity, GRP underfloor, and double-glazed tinted windows that open awning style.
The 420 floorplan comes in at 5.68 meters (18.6 feet) overall length, with 4.26 meters (14 feet) for the body and a width of 2.16 meters (7 feet). It's compact but not very small by European standards , but it's the only one to offer dual entries and cargo hauling capabilities.
The Beachy 420 has an extra-large entry door on the campsite side and a tailgate-style opening in the rear wall panel. This last one doubles as a loading area for gear, including larger items like motorcycles and bikes, which can be stored between the two benches at the back and secured with the provided tie-downs.
Photo: Hobby Caravan At camp, this opening is your oversize window onto whatever view you happen to be parked by, a way of inviting the great outdoors inside and a quick way out whenever you feel like it.
That's another thing that makes this caravan different from the rest, its outdoorsy character. Like its name says, the Beachy isn't designed to be lived in full time; it's more of a durable and cozy tent on wheels that will get you to the beach and provide you with an above-the-ground basecamp.
That explains its modularity and what could be perceived as a lack of basic creature comforts. The Beachy 420 is intentionally basic so you may spec it with exactly the things you need, and none of those you have no use for.
Photo: Hobby Caravan The kitchen space, for instance, is a mere worktop with a sink with only cold water and a larger slider drawer with a 12V cooler box underneath. Located at the very front of the trailer, it offers plenty of counter space for whatever appliance you want to bring along and sufficient storage for foodstuffs, pots and pans, and cutlery.
The closet angled to the side is both storage space and a rudimentary washroom in the 2027 UK version. It comes standard with a porta-potti and a large mirror, but also adjustable shelves and hanging space, so if you don't mind going number 2 under your finest beach dresses (or shirts), you will not have to rely on campground bathroom facilities when nature calls.
The rear of the trailer is taken up by two large benches in a face-to-face disposition. During the day, that's your dinette if you add the freestanding table, or your lounge. At night, you can use the space in several configurations: as twin beds, a double bed, or the super-size king that takes up the entire floorspace here.
Photo: Hobby Caravan As promised, the Beachy 420 offers ample storage options , in addition to the cabinets and open cubbies in the kitchen and the large closet slash toilet room. You also get two large pieces of furniture with fabric organizers and elasticated cables, and overhead cubbies on both sides. These come with more boxes and cables, so you can choose one you like best when packing.
The Beachy 420 comes with one-key locking system, a 25-liter (6.6-gallon) tank for freshwater in the closet, a rollable tank for wastewater, 12V, USB, and USB-C outlets, an opening skylight over the bed/living space, and beautiful pendant lights.
The European version offers options like a weight upgrade, a drawbar bike rack, special Beachy decals, a weather-proof aluminum storage box on the drawbar, a 230V electric heater with 1kW output, and pre-wiring for solar, and it could be that they will be available for the Aura variant as well. The textile boxes are optional in Europe, as is the toilet.
Photo: Hobby Caravan The Beachy 420 has an empty weight of about 842 kg (1,856 lbs) depending on options and a maximum permissible weight of 1,000 kg (2,204 lbs), which can be upgraded to 1,200 kg (2,645 lbs). The Aura variant will also come with Aura-branded upholstery and throw pillows in a nice golden sand color.
The unit brought to the trade event and toured below had a sticker of £20,995, which is roughly €25,100 or $28,100 at the current exchange rate.
